This allows a server to overwrite an existing local file specified in the Content-Disposition header despite the presence of the -J non-overwrite constraint.

Thus the problem is that when -J is used, curl should not overwrite existing files. But due to early hints or ETag handling, it might open the output file prematurely, bypassing the check.
